clue.text: Sam has real trouble in debtors' prison

indicators.note: having trouble suggests things in disorder, so these three words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A man called Sam with genuine money worries ends up behind bars for debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' signals an anagram of SAM HAS REAL; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marshalsea was a notorious London prison used largely for debtors, famously featured by Dickens.

clue.text: Acted quietly if one making entry dried up

indicators.note: the two short pieces go into the middle of the longer word, as if entering it

parts.note: mummers acted in dumb show, so to have mummed is to have acted silently
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An actor performing silently, wondering whether anyone will come in.
explanation.walkthrough: Mummers were folk actors who performed in dumb show, which is why 'acted quietly' fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A mummified body has been preserved by drying out, so mummified is a fanciful word for desiccated.

clue.text: Pay attention to detail

definitions.meaning: to heed or regard something, as when you honour someone's wishes
a particular point or aspect, as in 'in every way' or 'in this regard'

explanation.surface: An instruction to be careful about the small things.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning to heed or honour and a noun meaning a particular aspect or point.

clue.text: Liquid refreshment mother found in a northern town

indicators.note: the parent sits inside the other letters as if discovered there

parts.note: Sale is a town near Manchester in northern England
a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: A drink a mother tracked down in a town in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Sale is a town in Greater Manchester; Adam's ale is old slang, the first man having only water to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a jocular old name for plain water, the drink of the first man.

clue.text: Yen to have antique screens replaced before anniversary'

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put back in a different order

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: Someone longing to swap out old screens ahead of a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives SESQUICENTENAR; the yen symbol is added at the end. Sesqui- is Latin for one and a half.
explanation.definitionFit: A sesquicentenary is a hundred-and-fiftieth anniversary, from Latin sesqui meaning one and a half.

clue.text: William Tell, for one, was more roguish

definitions.meaning: the Swiss folk hero famous for shooting an apple off his son's head with a crossbow
comparative of arch, meaning mischievous or knowing

explanation.surface: The Swiss legend behaved with extra mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss hero was a bowman, and the comparative of arch (playfully sly) is spelt the same way.

clue.text: Involved in security, one may be shot

definitions.meaning: a sliding bar that fastens a door is part of keeping a home secure
a crossbow fires a short arrow, and a door's bar is also shot when slid home

explanation.surface: Someone in the security business who risks being fired upon.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a door fastener and a crossbow missile, and both are said to be shot.

clue.text: Dancer's unfinished poem about the Emerald Isle

definitions.note: read as 'dancer is', so the definition is just the dancer

indicators.note: the shortened poem goes around the poetic name for Ireland
the poem loses its final letter

parts.note: a ballad is a narrative poem or song
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland, nicknamed the Emerald Isle

explanation.surface: A dancer has an incomplete poem about Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' leaves BALLA, which then goes around the poetic name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a female ballet dancer.

clue.text: US city politician initially outraged about send-up

parts.note: LA stands for Los Angeles
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: take just the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: on means concerning, as in a talk on a topic

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles politician is incensed by a parody of himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampoon is a satirical attack, a synonym for a send-up or spoof.

clue.text: Deceives Yorkshire beauty queen verbally

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the phrase sounds like a different word

parts.note: the winner of a beauty contest for Leeds, a city in Yorkshire, would be Miss Leeds

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire pageant winner is caught out lying in her speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, northern England; beauty queens are styled 'Miss' plus their place.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislead someone is to give them a wrong impression, a direct synonym for deceive.

clue.text: Newspaper feature strongly supporting Nelson?

definitions.meaning: a regular article by a named writer in a paper
the tall pillar in Trafalgar Square holds up the statue of Admiral Nelson

explanation.surface: A newspaper article loudly backing Nelson.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson's statue stands atop a tall stone pillar in Trafalgar Square, London.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular newspaper piece and the London monument holding up the admiral share the same name.

clue.text: The thought of Parisian being arrested in Midwestern state

indicators.note: the French word is held inside the state abbreviation as if detained

parts.note: IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa
de is French for 'of'

explanation.surface: Imagine a Frenchman being arrested somewhere in the American Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The thought of' reads naturally together, but 'of' belongs with Parisian, giving the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or notion; 'The thought of' is how the surface reads but the definition is the thought itself.

clue.text: Music-maker using press accommodation in theatre

parts.note: to press something is to squeeze it
a box is a private compartment of seats in a theatre

explanation.surface: A musician makes use of a press box at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeezebox is an informal name for an accordion or concertina, an instrument that produces music.

clue.text: Rugby player goes to Bury to get engaged

indicators.note: the player is placed after the burial word, joining it at the end

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
a lock is a second-row forward in rugby

explanation.surface: A rugby forward travels to the Lancashire town of Bury to get engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town, but it is the verb meaning inter.
explanation.definitionFit: Interlocking parts fit together and engage with one another, as gears engage.

clue.text: Even-handed Italian in uniform

indicators.note: the abbreviation for Italian sits inside the word for uniform

parts.note: equable means steady and unvarying

explanation.surface: A fair-minded Italian wearing uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like a noun for clothing, but it is the adjective meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: An equitable person treats all sides fairly, so is even-handed.

clue.text: Crony has no right to identify addict

indicators.note: the companion word lacks the abbreviation for right

parts.note: a crony is a close friend

explanation.surface: A pal without a right identifies a drug user.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to identify' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend can mean an enthusiast or addict, as in a dope fiend or fresh-air fiend.

clue.text: It takes steady application to make a stagecoach

definitions.meaning: a public horse-drawn coach once used in France

explanation.surface: Becoming a coach driver requires hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It takes' and 'to make a' are links between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means persistent hard work and also a French public stagecoach of earlier centuries.

clue.text: Possible cause of a stirring in the leaves?

definitions.text: Possible cause of a stirring in the leaves?

parts.words: Possible cause of a stirring in the leaves?
parts.note: read as wind in a tree, but it means a small utensil swirling tea leaves in a cup

explanation.definitionFit: A small spoon used to stir a cup of tea would agitate the tea leaves in it.

clue.text: Union involved in obstruction? It's a fact

indicators.note: the union abbreviation is wrapped up inside the barrier word

parts.note: a dam is a barrier blocking water
TU stands for trade union

explanation.surface: Is the trade union involved in blocking things? It's true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information or fact, the singular of data.

clue.text: Soothing gesture unknown in an Eastern capital

indicators.note: the gesture and the unknown go inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
a nod is a gesture of the head
Y is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the capital letter of Eastern is E

explanation.surface: A calming wave of the hand by a stranger in an Asian capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters split as A-NODY-NE. 'Eastern capital' suggests a city such as Tokyo but just means the capital letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodyne describes something that soothes or relieves pain, from the Greek for painless.

clue.text: Worker way back engaging volunteers before delivery

parts.note: a worker ant is a classic crossword worker

indicators.note: the reversed road takes in the volunteer abbreviation
the road word is read backwards

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or way
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A worker heads back along a road, taking on volunteers before the delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives ENAL and taking in the volunteers makes ENATAL. The Territorial Army is the UK's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenatal means relating to pregnancy, the period before a baby is delivered.

clue.text: Short time as member of Ipswich, initially getting goals

parts.note: a term is a limited period, such as a school term
being in a club means being a member of it

indicators.note: take only the opening letter of the town

explanation.surface: A brief spell as a player for Ipswich brings goals.
explanation.walkthrough: Ipswich is an English town with a football club. 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are end points or destinations, so goals in the sense of places aimed for.

clue.text: Device English doctor used on the French motorway

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine degree
le is French for 'the'
M marks a British motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A doctor from England uses a gadget on a French autoroute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a device is an emblem or badge.

clue.text: Having no limits, unlike A Midsummer Night's Dream

definitions.meaning: without any end or bottom, unfathomable
Shakespeare's play features the weaver Bottom, so a version without him would lack Bottom

explanation.surface: Something boundless, quite different from a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom is the weaver who is given an ass's head in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means limitless or unfathomably deep, and humorously describes a play lacking its character Bottom.

clue.text: Ship's officer, briefly?

definitions.meaning: read as 'ship is': a two-masted sailing vessel
short for brigadier, an army officer

explanation.surface: A naval officer, given a short mention.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a two-masted sailing ship and the informal shortening of brigadier.

clue.text: It represents the sound of a percussion instrument

indicators.note: the instrument's name said out loud matches another word

parts.note: a cymbal is a brass plate struck in an orchestra

explanation.surface: A clashing brass instrument stands for its own noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol is a sign that stands for something else, so it represents.

clue.text: Endorsement from a party in top assembly

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: assembling the two short words means putting their letters together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A party's approval given at a meeting of top people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' signals an anagram of IN TOP, giving PTION; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption of a policy or proposal means its formal acceptance or endorsement.

clue.text: Present from another enthusiast

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A gift received from a fellow fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift but means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: To be here is to be present at a place, as in answering a register.

clue.text: Announced votes against joining county? Such sauce

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the phrase sounds like the dressing

parts.note: noes are nays, placed after Mayo, a county in the west of Ireland

explanation.surface: Votes against merging with a county are declared outrageous cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayo is a county in Ireland; MAYO with NAYS after it, said aloud, gives the sauce. 'Such sauce' plays on sauce meaning cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayonnaise is a cold sauce made from egg yolks and oil.
